title: Build 'safe house,' inquest jury advises
article: The five-day coroner's inquest into the Jan. 14, 2001 death of Maurice Linklater in Moosonee has returned six recommendations.
Linklater was fatally shot by Moosonee Ontario Provincial Police during a confrontation after he had been seen walking down a Moosonee street, firing a shotgun at a taxi cab and a light standard.
The jury, made up of Moosonee and Moose Factory residents, suggested the town of Moosonee consider building a safe house for the temporary lodging of intoxicated people.

The recommendations said the safe house would give intoxicated persons a safe environment and a viable option for police to putting them in jail. It also suggested the house would allow police manpower, cell space and operating dollars to be used more efficiently.
"I think the recommendations are quite thoughtful," said Ontario's deputy chief coroner for inquests, Bonita Porter.
